API Reference

Flask app

Flask app that shows the Grad Cafe analysis results.

class app.PullState

Bases: object

Remembers whether a data pull is running.

Tests can read or set busy directly instead of waiting on timing.

finish()

Mark the pull as finished.

try_start()

Mark a pull as running unless one already is.

Returns:

True if this caller started the pull, False if one was running.

app.build_analysis(database_url=None)

Ask the database every question and return the answers as text.

Parameters:

database_url – Optional URL that replaces DATABASE_URL.

Returns:

a list of dicts with the keys “number”, “question” and “answers” (plus “mine” for my own questions). Every answer starts with “Answer: “.

Return type:

A dict with one key, “questions”

app.create_app(config=None, scraper=None, loader=None, query_fn=None)

Build the Flask app.

Every argument is optional. Tests pass fakes so nothing touches the internet, and a test database URL through config.

Parameters:

  • config – Dict merged into app.config. Set “DATABASE_URL” here to use a different database than the DATABASE_URL environment variable.

  • scraper – Function with no arguments that returns raw records.

  • loader – Function that takes a list of row tuples and returns how many were added.

  • query_fn – Function with no arguments that returns the dict made by build_analysis.

Returns:

The configured Flask app. Its busy state is available as app.extensions[“pull_state”].

Scraper

Grad Cafe scraper: hybrid urllib3 (URL construction) + Selenium-attach (navigation).

scrape.main(argv=None)

Run the scraper from the command line.

Parameters:

argv – Optional list of command-line arguments. Uses sys.argv if None.

scrape.scrape_data(max_records: int = 40000, start_url: str = 'https://www.thegradcafe.com/survey/', raw_path: str = 'raw_scrape_progress.jsonl', state_path: str = 'raw_scrape_state.json', debugger_address: str = '127.0.0.1:9222') → list[dict]

Scrape applicant entries from The Grad Cafe, one page at a time, until max_records is reached or the site stops sending a next page.

Saves progress to raw_path and state_path after every page, so if this gets interrupted (rate limit, Chrome closing, etc.), running it again continues from where it stopped instead of starting over. If the Chrome tab itself crashes, it reconnects and tries again automatically (up to MAX_CONSECUTIVE_DRIVER_RETRIES times) before giving up. Any other kind of failure stops the scraper right away instead of retrying.

Cleaning

Structuring/cleaning helpers for raw Grad Cafe scrape output.

clean.clean_data(raw_records: list[dict]) → list[dict]

Convert raw scraped GradCafe records into the structured applicant_data.json schema.

clean.load_data(path: str) → list[dict]

Load a list of record dicts from a JSON file at path.

clean.main(argv=None)

Run the cleaning and LLM standardization steps from the command line.

Parameters:

argv – Optional list of command-line arguments. Uses sys.argv if None.

clean.save_data(records: list[dict], path: str) → None

Save a list of record dicts to path as valid JSON.

clean.standardize_names(records: list[dict], n_workers: int = 2, n_threads: int = 5, work_dir: str = '_llm_work') → list[dict]

Run all the records through app.py, split across n_workers processes at once, and add cleaned_program/cleaned_university to each one without changing anything else. If you stop this partway through, rerun it with the same n_workers number so it can pick up where it left off.

Loading data

Load the cleaned Grad Cafe applicant data into PostgreSQL.

load_data.clean_text(value)

Return the text stripped of spaces, or None if it is missing or blank.

load_data.create_table(conn)

Create the applicants table if it is not already there.

load_data.get_p_id(url)

Use the entry number at the end of the url as the id.

load_data.insert_rows(conn, rows)

Insert rows into applicants and return how many were really added.

A row whose p_id is already in the table is skipped, so running the loader again does not create duplicates.

load_data.load_rows(rows, database_url=None)

Create the table if needed and insert the rows in one transaction.

If anything fails, the connection is closed without a commit, so no partial writes are left behind.

Parameters:

  • rows – Row tuples in column order, as made by make_row.

  • database_url – Optional URL that replaces DATABASE_URL.

Returns:

How many rows were really added.

load_data.main()

Read the JSON file and load it into the applicants table.

load_data.make_nationality(value)

The source uses “0” when there is no classification, so store NULL.

load_data.make_program(program, university)

Join program and university into one text value, program first.

load_data.make_row(record)

Build one database row (a tuple in column order) from a JSON record.

Returns None if the record has no usable id.

load_data.read_records(path)

Read the list of applicant records from a JSON file.

load_data.to_float(value)

Turn a value like “3.40” into a float, or None if it is not a number.

load_data.to_score(value, low, high)

Like to_float, but zero and values outside low..high become None.

The source uses 0 when a score was left blank, and some people enter scores on a different scale (old GRE scores, GPAs out of 10), so those are treated as missing instead of being averaged in.

Pulling new data

Fetch newly posted Grad Cafe entries and add them to the database.

Run from the command line (or from the Flask page with the Pull Data button). Chrome must already be open with remote debugging on port 9222, the same setup as the Module 2 scraper.

pull_data.chrome_is_open()

Check that something is listening on Chrome’s debugging port.

Without this, a missing Chrome takes about a minute to be noticed.

Returns:

True if the port accepts a connection, otherwise False.

pull_data.fetch_new_raw_records(known_ids)

Read survey pages newest first and keep the entries we do not have.

Stops after the first page that has nothing new, since everything after it is older.

Parameters:

known_ids – The p_id values already in the database.

Returns:

A list of raw Grad Cafe records.

Raises:

RuntimeError – If robots.txt forbids scraping or a link leaves the site.

pull_data.get_known_ids(conn)

Return the set of p_id values already in the database.

pull_data.main()

Pull new entries. Returns 0 on success and 1 if something went wrong.

pull_data.run_pull(scraper, loader)

Scrape, clean and load new entries.

Parameters:

  • scraper – Function with no arguments that returns raw records.

  • loader – Function that takes a list of row tuples and returns how many were added.

Returns:

How many rows the loader added.

pull_data.scrape_new_records(database_url=None)

Scrape the entries that are not in the database yet.

This is the default scraper used by the Pull Data button.

Parameters:

database_url – Optional URL that replaces DATABASE_URL.

Returns:

A list of raw Grad Cafe records.

Raises:

RuntimeError – If Chrome is not open on the debugging port.

Querying with raw SQL

Answer the Grad Cafe analysis questions with raw SQL through psycopg.

query_data.fetch_all(conn, sql)

Run a query and give back every row it returns.

query_data.fetch_row(conn, sql)

Run a query that returns one row and give that row back.

query_data.fetch_value(conn, sql)

Run a query that returns a single value and give that value back.

query_data.main()

Run every query and print the answers.

query_data.show_average(value)

Two decimals, like 3.79.

query_data.show_count(value)

Whole number with commas, like 19,290.

query_data.show_percent(value)

Two decimals and a percent sign, like 50.09%.

Querying with SQLAlchemy

Answer some of the analysis questions again, using SQLAlchemy instead of SQL.

orm_queries.accepted_fall_2026_gpa(session)

Q6: average GPA of accepted Fall 2026 applicants.

orm_queries.american_fall_2026_gpa(session)

Q4: average GPA of American applicants for Fall 2026.

orm_queries.average_scores(session)

Q3: average GPA, GRE Quantitative, GRE Verbal and GRE Writing.

Each avg() skips NULLs on its own, so an applicant only counts toward the scores they gave.

orm_queries.fall_2025_acceptance_percent(session)

Q5: percent of Fall 2025 entries that are acceptances.

orm_queries.fall_2026_count(session)

Q1: how many entries are for Fall 2026.

orm_queries.gpa_by_decision(session)

Q11: average GPA of accepted vs rejected Fall 2026 applicants.

orm_queries.gre_by_nationality(session)

Q10: average GRE Quantitative for American vs International.

orm_queries.international_percent(session)

Q2: percent international among entries with a usable nationality.

orm_queries.jhu_masters_cs_count(session)

Q7: Johns Hopkins master’s Computer Science entries (original fields).

orm_queries.main()

Run the ORM queries and print the answers.

orm_queries.phd_cs_acceptance_count(session, program_column, university_column)

Q8 and Q9: Fall 2026 PhD Computer Science acceptances at four schools.

The program and university columns are passed in, so the same function works for the original fields (Q8) and the LLM-generated fields (Q9).

orm_queries.rounded_avg(column)

Average rounded to 2 decimals inside the database, like ROUND in SQL.

Rounding in the query keeps the numbers identical to the raw SQL ones.

orm_queries.show_average(value)

Two decimals, like 3.79.

orm_queries.show_count(value)

Whole number with commas, like 19,290.

orm_queries.show_percent(value)

Two decimals and a percent sign, like 50.09%.
